name: Northern Tlaxiaco Mixtec
world_status: statement found in an open source

earlier_scan.source_named: Gittlen, Laura 2016. Gramatica popular: Mixteco del norte de Tlaxiaco (SIL Mexico, 140pp grammar sketch; Glottolog MED). sil.org returned 403.

new_statements.quote: En el mixteco del norte de Tlaxiaco, las palabras básicas se componen de dos sílabas. La sílaba tónica o acentuada se pronuncia con más fuerza y siempre es la penúltima sílaba (antes de la última). [p.6] ... Las vocales cortadas por el saltillo aparecen solamente en la sílaba tónica de la palabra, es decir, en la sílaba que tiene mayor prominencia. En español la acentuación no es completamente regular ... Sin embargo, en mixteco, la acentuación es regular y predecible; el acento siempre recae sobre la penúltima sílaba de la palabra. [p.7]
new_statements.translation: In Northern Tlaxiaco Mixtec, basic words consist of two syllables. The tonic or stressed syllable is pronounced with more force and is always the penultimate syllable (the one before the last). ... Vowels cut by the glottal stop appear only in the tonic syllable of the word, i.e. the syllable with greatest prominence. In Spanish accentuation is not completely regular ... However, in Mixtec, accentuation is regular and predictable; the stress always falls on the penultimate syllable of the word.

new_statements.rule_in_words: Word stress is fixed on the penultimate syllable of the word (basic roots are disyllabic couplets, so stress = couplet-initial); glottalized/checked vowels are licensed only in the stressed syllable. Corroborated by Gittlen & Marlett 1985:176-177 'Primary word stress always falls on the penultimate syllable of the word in NM' with rule V -> [+stress] / __ (C0)V]word.
new_statements.exceptions: Reduced (truncated) first members of compounds lose their stress, the compound keeps penultimate stress (2016 p.8; 1985 p.188); in plural forms of directional motion verbs stress no longer falls on the root's tonic syllable but on the plural suffix -kuei, which itself has the penultimate pattern of a normal word (2016 p.15; 1985 p.189); monosyllabic dependent words/clitics do not stand alone. Language is also tonal (three levels: high, mid, low), tone unmarked in the practical orthography.
new_statements.domain_note: Domain is the (phonological) word including suffix -kuei and compounds; enclitic pronouns written as separate words. Description based on San Juan Ñumí speech.
new_statements.identity_note: Both sources describe the speech of San Juan Ñumí ('Ñumí Mixtec', NM), the reference variety for ISO xtn / Glottolog nort2985 Northern Tlaxiaco Mixtec; the SIL page notes the code also covers Santiago Nundiche, San Sebastián Nicananduta and San Antonino Monteverde with 'clear differences among them'.

La sílaba tónica o acentuada se pronuncia con más fuerza y siempre es la penúltima sílaba (antes de la última). [p.6] ... Las vocales cortadas por el saltillo aparecen solamente en la sílaba tónica de la palabra, es decir, en la sílaba que tiene mayor prominencia. sources.locator: Sec. 1.2 'Las palabras', p.6 and p.7 (PDF pp.12-13); also sec. 2.1(c) p.15
sources.note: Sec. 1.2 p.6: stressed syllable is always the penult; p.7: 'en mixteco, la acentuación es regular y predecible; el acento siempre recae sobre la penúltima sílaba de la palabra'; glottalized (checked) vowels occur only in the tonic syllable; p.8 reduced first members of compounds lose stress; p.15 in plural motion verbs stress moves to the plural suffix -kuei. Tone (high/mid/low) described separately, unmarked in orthography.

sources.citation: Gittlen, Laura and Stephen A. Marlett. 1985. Ñumí Mixtec syllable structure and morphology. Work Papers of the Summer Institute of Linguistics, University of North Dakota Session 29: 175-194. DOI 10.31356/silwp.vol29.03
sources.note: p.176-177: 'Primary word stress always falls on the penultimate syllable of the word in NM.' with formal rule (5) Stress Assignment V -> [+stress] / __ (C0)V]X0; checked (glottalized) vowels and two-segment onsets only in the stressed syllable; p.188 truncated compound stems lose stress, penultimate stress of the compound maintained; p.189 plural kwei 'has the penultimate stress pattern of a normal word'. Tone analysis stated to be incomplete.
